stem: An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department after a playground collision and an upper central incisor has been avulsed; which interpretation is most likely?

options.text: It is more likely a primary tooth because primary teeth erupt from 6 to 18 years
It is more likely a permanent tooth because permanent teeth erupt from 6 to 18 years
Tooth type cannot be inferred because both dentitions are fully erupted by 3 years
It is abnormal because permanent teeth do not erupt until adulthood
It is most likely a supernumerary tooth because extra teeth are expected in normal development

explanation: Permanent tooth. At 8 years, an erupted upper central incisor is more likely to be permanent because permanent teeth erupt from 6 to 18 years.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Normal dental development; Oro-Facial Trauma

rationale: Primary teeth erupt between 6 and 36 months; permanent teeth erupt from 6 to 18 years; the maxillary central incisor is commonly involved in oro-facial trauma.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because primary teeth erupt between 6 and 36 months, not from 6 to 18 years
optionExplanations.B: Correct because at 8 years an erupted upper central incisor is more likely to be a permanent tooth, as permanent teeth erupt from 6 to 18 years
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because age does help distinguish primary from permanent dentition, and 8 years falls within the permanent eruption range
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because permanent teeth do erupt during childhood and adolescence, not only in adulthood
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because supernumerary teeth are not the expected normal explanation for an erupted upper central incisor
